newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms late, interbank rate down further.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms late, interbank rate down further.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed against the dollar in late trade on Thursday following the U.S. weakness abroad, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 25.935/25.940 to the dollar late from 25.950/25.955 in early morning trade, dealers said.
Dealers said the dollar's weakness against the baht was supported by some dollar buying due to ample liquidity.
"There was some bids for the dollar. The money supply was very high," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.94 per dollar against 25.93 on Wednesday.

The overnight interbank rate fell further to 6.25-7.00 percent late from 8.50-9.00 despite the Bank of Thailand's annoucement of an additional issue it would increase its bond auction on Friday to mop up excess liquidity, dealers said.
"There was very little reaction in the market from the news. The liquidity continued to rise today," said one money market dealer.

The Bank of Thailand said it sharply raised its March 21, one-month weekly bond auction to 20 billion baht from a previously planned two billion baht in order to curb expected excess liquidity later this month.

A central bank statement said the decision was a preemptive move against anticipated higher liquidity in the banking system after a scheduled withdrawal of about 70-80 billion baht of start-up funds by the Government Pension Fund on March 27.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 9.00/10.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 8.70/9.20 earlier.
